prompt:
I need the front end for Kidney Kin. A low-cost messaging service run by a volunteer kidney transplant peer support network, where trained recipient mentors keep in touch with people on the transplant waitlist and can bring in volunteer clinical advisors with the patient's consent.

Who's using it: Gloria Hutchins, 64, a retired elementary school teacher who is six years past her own kidney transplant. She volunteers as a peer mentor for four people at different stages on the waitlist. She completed the network's 8-hour mentor training. She is not a clinician and is careful not to sound like one.

What they're doing right now: She opened the app at breakfast to a message sent at 11:40 last night by her newest mentee, Darnell, 41, who is on dialysis. A potential living donor's crossmatch came back positive, the clinic said they'd 'talk about options', and he's frightened it means he's lost his chance. Gloria wants to reply warmly from her own experience without giving medical advice. Darnell agreed at intake to have clinical questions shared, so she also wants to bring in the network's volunteer clinical advisor, a retired transplant nurse. She also has a reply owed to another mentee from three days ago, and the network coordinator has posted a reminder about the December mentor call.

What's in the system at this point: Gloria's four mentee conversations: Darnell Price (matched Oct 2026, 23 messages, consent to involve a clinical advisor: yes), Mei-Ling Cho (matched Mar 2026, 140 messages, last reply from Gloria 3 days ago, consent: no), Arturo Vega (matched Jan 2026, in 'quiet' status at his request), and Pat Gorman (transplanted Sep 2026, transitioning out of mentorship). The network has 3 volunteer clinical advisors with their availability hours and a coordinator account. Mentor guideline excerpts are kept on hand, e.g., 'Share experience, not advice' and 'Escalate if mentee mentions self-harm'. There is a group thread for 31 active mentors and an announcement for the Dec 9 mentor call at 7 pm. The network's message volume is about 600 a month.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
